content.title: Infections in patients with heart failure - key points
recommendations: Patients with HF are at increased risk of infections and have poorer outcomes once infected.
Telemonitoring avoids the risks of infections caused by close contact and is useful during pandemic conditions; it may be implemented for patient follow-up.
During pandemics, HF patients should be screened for infection at the time of hospitalization, for urgent admissions, or before elective hospitalizations.

Careful assessment of fluid status in addition to clinical signs of HF is mandatory during hospitalization in patients with concomitant sepsis; echocardiography measures (eg, IVC diameter/collapsibility) may be used.

Continue optimal medical therapy (OMT) in chronic HF patients whenever blood pressure and haemodynamic conditions permit, considering drug interactions with infection-related therapies and side effect profiles.
OMT_components: ARB (angiotensin-receptor blocker) or ARNI (angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor)
content.source_notes: Table/section repeated in the page; recommendations emphasize infection risk in HF and continuation of guideline-directed HF therapies while considering infection-related interactions.

Associated Conditions: Heart failure (treatment target via ACE inhibitors)
genes.context: OMT (including ... ACE-I ...) and abbreviation: 'ACE-I = angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor' — ACE is the target of ACE inhibitors used in HF.
OMT lists 'ARB or ARNI' and abbreviation: 'ARB = angiotensin-receptor blocker' — angiotensin II receptor type 1 (AGTR1) is the common angiotensin receptor targeted in HF therapy.

Associated Conditions: Heart failure (neprilysin is targeted by ARNIs)
genes.context: Abbreviation: 'ARNI = angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor' — neprilysin (MME) is the neprilysin enzyme component referenced in ARNI therapy.

Associated Conditions: Heart failure (targeted by mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists)
genes.context: OMT includes 'MRA' and abbreviation: 'MRA = mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist' — the mineralocorticoid receptor is encoded by NR3C2 and is targeted in HF treatment.
OMT includes 'SGLT2 inhibitors' and abbreviation: 'SGLT2 = sodium-glucose co-transporter 2' — SGLT2 corresponds to the SLC5A2 gene product targeted in HF therapies.
OMT lists 'beta-blocker' as a component of therapy — beta-1 adrenergic receptor (ADRB1) is a principal cardiac beta-adrenergic receptor targeted by beta-blockers in HF.
